title: Climate Talks End With No Deal
summary: Big climate talks in Turkey ended on Sunday with no deal at all. The meeting, called COP31, went on for more than two weeks. It was the longest climate meeting ever held by the United Nations. Nearly 200 countries sent people to take part. Each year, countries meet to agree on ways to slow global warming. This time, they could not agree. The talks went on past Friday's deadline, but still no deal came. The European Union and other countries said no to a draft plan from Turkey and Australia. The plan did not mention fossil fuels at all. Fossil fuels are the main cause of global warming, scientists say, so the EU would not back a deal that left them out. Turkey's meeting leader, Murat Kurum, said there would be no new plan. With no deal, there will be no new help for countries hit hardest by climate disasters. There will also be no new steps to keep warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius, the goal set in 2015. It was the first time climate talks have failed since 2009.
why_it_matters: When countries cannot agree on slowing global warming, the weather around you can keep getting hotter and storms can get stronger.

background_read: Each year, countries around the world meet to talk about how to slow global warming.
These big meetings are called climate talks, and this one was named COP31.
This time the talks ended with no deal because the countries could not agree on what to do about fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
